workflow.remark: Corrections to paper_draft.tex, no new analysis: (1) Title: 'Rich Cores and Poor Peripheries' contradicts the paper's own finding (the clustering is national blocks; within countries none). Use a plain descriptive title, e.g. 'Spatial clustering of GDP per inhabitant across EU NUTS-2 regions, 2024'. (2) Abstract: there are three alternative weights (5 and 8 nearest neighbours, inverse distance), not four; the abstract's local clusters are uncorrected - add that after the false discovery rate correction 22 remain (20 low-low, one high-high, one high-low). (3) Introduction: 'the richest tenth of regions earns roughly 2.4 times the income of the poorest tenth' is wrong; say the 90th percentile is 2.4 times the 10th. (4) Local clusters: delete 'because the richest regions are fewer and more heterogeneous' (not tested). (5) Capital regions: the 27 dropped include whole single-region countries (EE00, LV00, LU00, CY00, MT00), and the drop leaves 3 regions without a neighbour (1 in the top-five variant); say both, and present 'income peaks surrounded by poorer neighbours' as a reading, not a finding. (6) Discussion: the demeaned Moran's I (0.020, p = 0.6) shows that regions' deviations from their national mean are not clustered; it does not test cross-border gradients - rewrite the sentence about 'cross-border gradients that a smooth core-periphery narrative would imply'. (7) Data: name the datasets (nama_10r_2gdp, unit PPS_EU27_2020_HAB; demo_r_d2jan) and add the sentence Eurostat's terms ask for: the statistics are computed by the authors from Eurostat data; Eurostat is not responsible for them. Keep the EuroGeographics notice in every map caption.
